edge_denoise · MIIC-burst-p10-dedup · val split · 2026-09-04

Target Ladder Plates

The real frames, crops, targets, outputs and σ maps behind the gradient-target ladder and its compute-matched controls.

Three workflows feed the numbers in the ladder report: a data workflow that turns one clean SEM image into sixteen synthetic noisy replicas, a training workflow that fine-tunes one network per arm on 64 px crops of those replicas, and an evaluation workflow that denoises ten replicas of each held-out scene and measures how much the results disagree. Every image below is taken from those runs on the same three validation scenes: src 48 (a typical bar), src 21 (harder), and src 87 (the one-site scene that decides the statistics). The amber marks on micrographs are the harness’s own measurement boxes.

1 · Data2 · Training3 · Evaluation4 · Result

1 · Data: one clean image becomes sixteen noisy frames

The corpus is synthetic on purpose: each 512 × 512 clean capture is turned into 16 independent Poisson replicas at an effective peak of 10 electrons per pixel, so the same content exists with different noise and the clean image is known. Every number in the report is measured on the 64 px centre crop, boxed in amber.

Plate 1

The frame, one replica, and the long average

Left to right: the clean capture, what a single peak-10 frame looks like, and the average of all sixteen. Averaging is the classical route to precision and it costs 16× the dose. The amber box is the region every later plate shows.

Plate 2

The classical ladder on the evaluation crop

Each doubling of the dose buys about 3 dB. The bar’s edges only become readable by eye around avg-of-8; the denoisers below have to do at least that well from a single frame.

2 · Training: what each arm is asked to match

Every arm sees the same input: one noisy replica of a random 64 px crop. The image term always matches a second, different replica (Noise2Noise). The arms differ only in what the gradient term chases, computed with the Sobel operator S, and in whether an agreement term ties the outputs of two replicas together. The next plate shows one crop under all of those targets.

Plate 3

One training crop and the four gradient targets

images the terms see (model range shown as intensity)
their Sobel gradients — the gradient term compares S(output) with one of these
|S| magnitude, same scale in every panel:0 → 0.53

Read the bottom row left to right as the ladder: the fresh-frame target is gradient noise with an edge hidden in it, the 15-frame mean has a quarter of that noise, the clean image has none, and the teacher average is clean but carries whatever the teacher gets wrong. The report’s finding is that going down this row did not improve precision against the control; only the agreement term (third tile, top row) did.

All ft_ arms start from the teacher’s weights and train 10,000 steps (ft_noisy_20k: 20,000; ft_noisy_b16: batch 16). The weights are λ_image = 1 and λ_gradient = 4 everywhere the terms appear.

Plate 5

Why the distillation target inherits the teacher

error against the clean image, same diverging scale
−0.08+0.08 (intensity)

Averaging sixteen teacher outputs barely changes the error map: RMS 0.014 → 0.012. The teacher’s error is mostly systematic, the same pattern on every replica, so the average keeps it. That is the “bias is inherited” prediction, seen directly.

3 · Evaluation: ten replicas in, ten answers out, how much do they disagree?

For each scene the harness feeds the first ten replicas of the crop through an arm and keeps the ten outputs. The per-pixel standard deviation across those ten outputs is the σ map: dark where the answer depends on the noise that happened to be in the input. Critical dimension (CD) is then measured on every output at sites chosen once on the clean image, and the spread of those measurements is the CD σ.

Plate 6

Every arm on src 48: output on seed 0, and its σ map

σ map (lower image in each tile), per-pixel σ across 10 seeds:0 → 0.03

The outputs are hard to tell apart by eye; the σ maps are not. Variance lives on the two edges of the bar for every arm, which is why PSNR is a poor guide to metrology precision. ft_consist’s σ map is visibly the lightest, and its pixel σ is a third lower than any control; the two compute-matched controls (ft_noisy_20k, ft_noisy_b16) look like ft_noisy.

Plate 7

The control, the compute-matched control, and ft_consist on the two hard scenes

src 21 — four sites, two of which are hard for every arm
src 87 — one site, the outlier scene

Same story on src 21: ft_consist’s σ map is the lightest. On src 87 the structure is a faint, wide feature; every arm’s σ map is dark along its edges, and the difference between arms is small.

Plate 8

How one CD number is made

clean profileft_noisy_b16, 10 seedsft_consist, 10 seeds
site 1, src 48clean CDmean CDCD 3σ
ft_noisy_b1621.42 px22.03 px0.416 px
ft_consist21.42 px22.06 px0.281 px

Inside a site’s box the rows are averaged into a profile (thick black: the clean image). A 50 % threshold is drawn between the profile’s low and high levels, and the two crossings nearest the clean edges, within the shaded ±4 px windows, are the edges; CD is their distance. The ticks under the axis are the ten seeds’ crossings for each arm: their spread is the CD σ. ft_consist’s ticks cluster more tightly.

Plate 9

Src 87: why three of ten measurements fail under ft_consist

clean profileft_noisy_b16ft_consistft_consist seeds with no valid crossing
ft_consist, all ten seeds, the site box drawn on each output

The feature is a low-contrast step, so the 50 % threshold sits close to the profile over a long stretch and the crossing wanders. Under ft_consist three seeds put the crossing outside the ±4 px window (amber profiles) and are dropped; the remaining seven give a σ no better than the controls. This single site, on the single-site scene, is the whole difference between “9 of 10 scenes” and the paired t-test’s p ≈ .2. Whether the smoother profile is a blur signature is the open question for the smoothness diagnostic.

4 · Result: per-scene CD 3σ for the control, its compute-matched twin, and ft_consist

Each row is one validation scene; the log axis lets the eight easy scenes and the two hard ones share a chart. ft_noisy_b16 costs the same per step as ft_consist, so the distance between the orange and the aqua mark is the consistency term’s effect at matched compute.

Nine of ten rows put the aqua mark left of the orange one. The exception is src 87, the scene of Plate 9. Doubling the control’s compute moved its marks a little and its pixel σ almost not at all; the consistency term moved pixel σ by a quarter and CD by about 0.1 px on the well-measured scenes. With one training seed that is a strong result, not an established one; the λ_c sweep with seeds is what settles it.
